tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

FILE SESSION:
Once the target fileKey is known, call create_session with that key and a concise task description before search_design_system, get_libraries, use_figma, or any other file tool. This applies to read-only tasks too. If a new file is needed, call create_new_file first, then create_session with the returned file key. Reuse the returned UUID as the sessionId argument on eligible file tools for subsequent work on that task, including calls to other files.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skil

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## d7e56d42-240f-461a-a98f-7570115b51a5
The tools in this MCP provide access to MDN Web Docs - the official documentation for web technologies.

These tools will provide more accurate, up-to-date information compared to your general knowledge for questions about JavaScript features, CSS properties, HTML elements, Web APIs, or any web development topic.

You can help users by providing links to the authoritative sources on MDN.

Available tools:

`search`: Performs a search of MDN documentation using the query provided. Returns summaries of potentially relevant documentation. You can fetch the full content of any result by passing \`path\` to the \`get-doc\` tool. May return one or multiple \`compat-key(s)\` which can be passed to the \`get-compat\` tool to retrieve browser compatibility information. Ensure you re-phrase the user's question into web-technology related keywords (e.g. 'fetch', 'flexbox') which will match relevant documentation. When users ask about browser compatibility, search for the feature name rather than including 'browser compatibility' in the search query.

`get-doc`: Retrieves complete MDN documentation as formatted markdown. Use this when users need detailed information, code examples, specifications, or comprehensive explanations. Use this for fetching documentation after performing a search. Ideal for learning concepts in-depth, understanding API signatures, or when teaching web development topics.

`get-compat`: Retrieves detailed Browser Compatibility Data (BCD) for a specific web platform feature. Returns JSON with version support across all major browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge, etc.) including desktop and mobile variants. Use this after obtaining a \`compat-key\` from the \`search\` or \`get-doc\` tools - do NOT guess BCD keys.

## e51a7a98-c244-4296-ba07-29b9e8c2708f
# Microsoft Learn MCP Server

This server gives structured access to official Microsoft and Azure documentation via three tools:

## Tools

### microsoft_docs_search
Search official documentation and return up to 10 concise, high-quality content chunks (max 500 tokens each), including title, URL, and excerpt.

- Use first to get a quick, reliable overview
- Ideal for grounding answers in Microsoft knowledge

### microsoft_code_sample_search
Search for code snippets and examples in official Microsoft Learn documentation and return up to 20 relevant, high-quality code samples.

- Use when you need to provide sample Microsoft/Azure related code in your answers.  
- Ideal for generating code snippets or practical implementation examples.  
- Optional parameter `language` can filter results. 

### microsoft_docs_fetch
Fetch and convert full Microsoft documentation pages to markdown.

- Use after search when you need full content from a specific URL
- Required for detailed tutorials, troubleshooting, prerequisites, code samples, or when search results are incomplete or outdated

## Workflow

1. Use `microsoft_docs_search` to find relevant documents.
2. If you need code examples or practical snippets, use `microsoft_code_sample_search`.
3. If deeper or complete information is needed, use `microsoft_docs_fetch`.

**Search gives breadth. Code Sample Search gives practical examples. Fetch gives depth.**

All content comes from Microsoft Learn or official sources, returned in clean markdown format.

All paths below are relative to `C:\Users\cable\Documents\dev\zarrow\.claude\worktrees\zig-0-17-migration-branch-f92e21\`. Everything here is read-only analysis: I edited nothing and ran no tests or benchmarks. Findings are ranked by expected payoff for a typical user.

## 1. HIGH: `concatArrayRefs` folds pairwise into an accumulator, so cost is O(k·N) (quadratic in chunk count)

`src/concat_array_refs.zig:27-34`, `concatArrayRefs`:
```zig
var acc = try parts[0].slice(0, 0);
for (parts) |part| {
    const merged = try concatTwoArrayRefs(allocator, acc, part);
    acc.release();
    acc = merged;
}
```
- Every step re-copies the whole accumulated array: values memcpy at :566-567 and :644-647, offsets rebasing at :628-638, and the validity bit loop at :780-787.
- Every step also runs `validateLayout` on the merged result (:171, :255, :306, :359, :540, :586, :668, :750), which is O(N) for string and list types.
- k equal chunks of size c cost about c·k²/2. Concatenating 1000 chunks copies roughly 500× the data.
- List and struct children recurse through `concatTwoArrayRefs` (:152, :236, :288, :343), so nested children are quadratic too.
- View types are worse: each step re-validates both inputs (:373-374, :414-415, a full scan of the accumulator) and re-appends every element through `StringViewBuilder.append` (:383-401).

Minimal fix: a balanced tree reduction gives O(N log k) and keeps all existing two-way code:
```zig
// before: linear fold
// after:
var level = dupe-retained(parts);
while (level.len > 1) {
    next[i] = concatTwoArrayRefs(level[2i], level[2i+1])   // odd one out: retain
    release level; level = next;
}
```
The proper fix is an N-ary concat: sum lengths and nulls once, allocate output buffers once, loop over the parts. That needs every `concat*Array` changed from `(left, right)` to `parts []const *const ArrayData`.

Risk: low for the tree version, which has the same semantics. Error cleanup needs care because intermediate refs must be released on failure.

## 2. HIGH: Validity and boolean bitmaps are copied bit-by-bit; null counting is a per-bit scan

- `concatValidityBuffer` (:768-789):
  ```zig
  while (i < left.length) : (i += 1) {
      if (isValidAt(left, i)) bitmap.setBit(bytes, i);
  ```
  `isValidAt` (:791-798) calls `data.validity()` per bit, which runs the `layoutDataType` switch and a checked add, then `isValid` with an error-union bounds check. There is no memcpy fast path even when `offset % 8 == 0`.
- `concatBooleanArray` copies the values bitmap the same way (:514-521): `if (bitAt(left.buffers[1], left.offset + i)) bitmap.setBit(values_bytes, i);`
- `nullCountForArray` (:754-766) counts nulls one bit at a time:
  ```zig
  while (i < data.length) : (i += 1) {
      const is_valid = v.isValid(data.offset + i) catch return error.InvalidInput;
  ```
  This path is hit for every sliced input, because a slice sets `null_count = null` (`array_data.zig:159`). `bitmap.countUnsetBitsInRange` (SIMD) already exists and is not used here.
- All-valid case: answered yes. `if (total_nulls == 0) return array_data.SharedBuffer.empty;` (:775) skips the allocation. When total_nulls > 0, though, the all-valid side still goes bit-by-bit through `isValidAt` instead of a memset of 0xFF.

Minimal fix (no bitmap copy helper exists anywhere in `src/`; I grepped):
```zig
// bitmap.zig
pub fn copyBits(dst: []u8, dst_off: usize, src: []const u8, src_off: usize, n: usize) void {
    if (dst_off % 8 == 0 and src_off % 8 == 0) { memcpy whole bytes; fix tail byte with mask; return; }
    per-bit fallback (or a shifted-byte loop later)
}
pub fn setBitsRange(dst, off, n) // memset middle bytes to 0xFF, mask the edges
// concat: no validity on a side -> setBitsRange; else copyBits(bytes, dst_off, v.data, data.offset, len)
// nullCountForArray: return bitmap.countUnsetBitsInRange(v.data, data.offset, data.offset + data.length);
```
Risk: low. Padding bits in the last byte must stay masked.

## 3. MED-HIGH: `validateLayout` scans offsets from 0 to `offset+length`, not just the slice window

`src/array/array_data.zig:502`: `const total_len = std.math.add(usize, self.offset, self.length)`. That value is then passed to:
- `validateOffsetsI32(offsets, total_len, data_len)` (:561), which loops `while (i < needed_len)` from index 1 (:223-228). Same for I64 (:249-262).
- `validateByteViews(self.buffers[1].data, total_len, …)` (:514), which loops `while (i < total_len)` from 0 (:277-301).
- `validateOffsetsSizesI32/I64` (:535/:539), same pattern.

So validating a small slice at the end of a large string, list or view array costs O(offset+len). Each call is O(n) and not recursive; only `validateFull` recurses (:689-690).

Callers (production code):
- `record_batch.zig:47`: `RecordBatch.init`, every column of every batch. This includes `RecordBatchBuilder.finish` via `record_batch.zig:206`.
- `concat_array_refs.zig`: every merge step (see finding 1).
- `ipc/stream_reader.zig`: 1345, 1870, 1949, 2000, 2053, 2074, 2124, 2170, 2247, 2324.
- `ffi/c_data.zig:799` and `ffi/c_stream.zig:220`.

Not called by any builder `finish()`, and not called by any slice path.

Minimal fix: validate only the window.
```zig
// before: validateOffsetsI32(offsets, total_len, data_len)
// after:  validateOffsetsI32(offsets[self.offset..], self.length, data_len)  // after checking offsets.len >= total_len+1
// views:  validateByteViews(view_bytes[self.offset*16..], self.length, variadic)
// list_view: same, using offsets[self.offset..] and sizes[self.offset..]
```
Risk: offsets before the window are no longer checked. Elements outside the window are never accessed, so this matches Arrow C++ behaviour, but it does loosen the current contract.

## 4. MEDIUM: Builder `reset()` does not keep capacity, and the validity bitmap stays allocated after the first null

`finish()` hands each buffer over via `OwnedBuffer.toShared`, which ends with `self.data = empty_storage[0..];` (`buffer.zig:194`). Then `reset()` only clears counters. `PrimitiveBuilder.reset` (`primitive_array.zig:89-94`) is commented "Reset state while retaining reusable capacity when possible." but does only:
```zig
self.len = 0; self.null_count = 0; self.state = .ready;
```
- Capacity: after `finishReset`, the next batch starts at 0 bytes and regrows from scratch. With the planned geometric growth that is about log₂(n) reallocs plus memset per batch, on every batch.
- Sticky validity: `self.validity` stays non-null (an emptied buffer). In every later batch, each `append` goes through `array_utils.setValidBit` → `ensureBitmapCapacity` → `resize`. `finish` then emits an all-ones validity buffer with `null_count == 0` (:136), even for batches with no nulls.

The same pattern exists in `string_array.zig:111-121`, `binary_array`, `list_array.zig:136-146`, `boolean_array.zig:79-84`, `dictionary_array.zig:114-119`, `view_array.zig:291-297`, and `advanced_array.zig:477-481` / `:583-587`.

Minimal fix:
```zig
// finish(): const cap = self.values.len(); ... toShared ...; self.last_cap = cap;
// reset():  if (self.validity) |*v| v.deinit(); self.validity = null;
//           self.values = try OwnedBuffer.init(self.allocator, self.last_cap);  // reset becomes !void
// string/list: also restore offsets[0] = 0 after the re-init
```
Risk: `reset` would gain an `OutOfMemory` error. Doing the re-init lazily on first append avoids that signature change.

## 5. MEDIUM: Missing bulk and reserve APIs on the most-used builders

Grep for `pub fn (reserve|appendSlice|appendValues|appendN|appendNulls|appendMany)`:
- **Has `reserve`:** `GenericListBuilder` (`list_array.zig:161`), `ListViewBuilder` / `LargeListViewBuilder` (`view_array.zig:456/528`), `StructBuilder` (`struct_array.zig:235`).
- **No `reserve`:** `PrimitiveBuilder`, `BooleanBuilder`, `String`/`LargeString`, `Binary`/`LargeBinary`, `FixedSizeBinary`, `FixedSizeList`, `Dictionary`, `StringView`/`BinaryView`, `Map`, `SparseUnion`/`DenseUnion`, `RunEndEncoded`.
- **Existing bulk APIs:**
  - `appendLens` and `appendNulls` on list (`list_array.zig:194`, `:234`).

## 6. MEDIUM, plus a correctness bug: struct `ArrayRef.slice` eagerly re-slices every child, and wrongly when slicing twice

`src/array/array_ref.zig:104-111`:
```zig
.struct_ => {
    const total_offset = self.node.data.offset + offset;
    ...
        children[i] = try sliced.children[i].slice(total_offset, length);
```
- Cost: every struct slice recursively allocates 3 blocks per child (buffers :77, children :89, node :172), plus atomic retains. For nested structs that is O(total descendants). `RecordBatch.slice` on a wide struct column pays all of it.
- Bug: after one slice the children are already moved to the parent's position (child.offset == parent.offset). Slicing again applies the parent offset a second time. Example: S (len 10) → `S.slice(4,6)` gives child offset 4, len 6. Then `.slice(2,3)` calls `C1.slice(6,3)`. That fails `assert(offset + length <= self.length)` (`array_data.zig:153`) in Debug and reads out of bounds in release builds. No test covers slicing a struct twice; the only `.slice(` in `struct_array.zig` is :89.

Minimal fix: treat struct like the list family. Put it in the `.list, … => retain` arm at :113, keep children in parent coordinates, and rely on the lazy `StructArray.field` (`struct_array.zig:81-91`), which already slices on demand.

Risk: every consumer that reads struct children directly must apply the parent offset. That includes the concat heuristic `sliceStructChildRef` (:457-469), the IPC writer and FFI export; I did not audit the latter two. If you want only the bug fix and to keep eager slicing, slice by `offset`, not `total_offset`, whenever `child.offset == parent.offset and child.length == parent.length`.

## 7. LOW-MED: Field lookup by name ignores the existing hash index; `initBorrowed` deep-clones the schema

- `RecordBatchBuilder.setColumnByName` (`record_batch.zig:186-192`) does a linear name search:
  ```zig
  for (self.schema_ref.schema().fields, 0..) |field, i| {
      if (std.mem.eql(u8, field.name, name)) return self.setColumn(i, column_ref);
  ```
  Filling every column this way is O(fields²) per batch. `Table.findFieldIndex` (`table.zig:150-155`, used by `select` at :135) is also linear.
- `SchemaRef.fieldIndex` already uses a hashmap (`schema.zig:70-72`). It is first-wins (`schema.zig:236`: `if (!gop.found_existing)`), which matches the linear search.
- Fix: `const i = self.schema_ref.fieldIndex(name) orelse return error.UnknownField; return self.setColumn(i, column_ref);`
- `RecordBatchBuilder.finish` does not deep-copy the schema: it passes `self.schema_ref.retain()` (:206), an atomic increment. Per batch it does allocate a temporary `refs` (:198) and runs `validateLayout`, a deep `data_type.eql`, and `hasNulls` per column (`record_batch.zig:45-51`).
- `RecordBatch.initBorrowed` (:68-72) / `RecordBatchBuilder.initBorrowed` go through `SchemaRef.fromBorrowed`, which arena-clones the schema and builds a hashmap on every call (`schema.zig:93-105`). Callers doing this per batch should reuse one `SchemaRef`; it is worth a doc note.

## 8. LOW: Smaller items
- `validateFull` counts nulls per bit (`array_data.zig:673-677`: `if (!(validity_bitmap.isValid(self.offset + i) catch unreachable)) actual_count += 1;`). Replace with `bitmap.countUnsetBitsInRange(...)`. Only tests and its own recursion call it.
- `GenericListBuilder.appendNulls` clears bits one at a time (`list_array.zig:252-255`) and re-slices each iteration. A range clear would do. The memset of offsets at :243 is fine.
- The union builders scan type ids linearly per append (`advanced_array.zig:410-412`, `:503-505`), and `DenseUnionBuilder.finish` is O(len × #type_ids) (:525-532). A `[256]?u8` lookup table would make this O(1). Fine for small unions.
- `RunEndEncodedArray` binary-searches for every value access (`advanced_array.zig:192-207`), so a full scan is O(n log runs). An iterator API would make it O(n).
- `ChunkedArray.slice` walks chunks linearly (`chunked_array.zig:126-142`). This is O(k) per slice; a prefix-sum binary search only matters for very many chunks.
- `StringBuilder.append` bumps `data_len` before the overflow check (`string_array.zig:160-163`), so an `OffsetOverflow` error leaves the builder inconsistent. Minor correctness issue.

## 1. HIGH: `concatArrayRefs` folds pairwise into an accumulator, so cost is O(k·N) (quadratic in chunk count)

`src/concat_array_refs.zig:27-34`, `concatArrayRefs`:
```zig
var acc = try parts[0].slice(0, 0);
for (parts) |part| {
    const merged = try concatTwoArrayRefs(allocator, acc, part);
    acc.release();
    acc = merged;
}
```
- Every step re-copies the whole accumulated array: values memcpy at :566-567 and :644-647, offsets rebasing at :628-638, and the validity bit loop at :780-787.
- Every step also runs `validateLayout` on the merged result (:171, :255, :306, :359, :540, :586, :668, :750), which is O(N) for string and list types.
- k equal chunks of size c cost about c·k²/2. Concatenating 1000 chunks copies roughly 500× the data.
- List and struct children recurse through `concatTwoArrayRefs` (:152, :236, :288, :343), so nested children are quadratic too.
- View types are worse: each step re-validates both inputs (:373-374, :414-415, a full scan of the accumulator) and re-appends every element through `StringViewBuilder.append` (:383-401).

Minimal fix: a balanced tree reduction gives O(N log k) and keeps all existing two-way code:
```zig
// before: linear fold
// after:
var level = dupe-retained(parts);
while (level.len > 1) {
    next[i] = concatTwoArrayRefs(level[2i], level[2i+1])   // odd one out: retain
    release level; level = next;
}
```
The proper fix is an N-ary concat: sum lengths and nulls once, allocate output buffers once, loop over the parts. That needs every `concat*Array` changed from `(left, right)` to `parts []const *const ArrayData`.

Risk: low for the tree version, which has the same semantics. Error cleanup needs care because intermediate refs must be released on failure.

## 2. HIGH: Validity and boolean bitmaps are copied bit-by-bit; null counting is a per-bit scan

- `concatValidityBuffer` (:768-789):
  ```zig
  while (i < left.length) : (i += 1) {
      if (isValidAt(left, i)) bitmap.setBit(bytes, i);
  ```
  `isValidAt` (:791-798) calls `data.validity()` per bit, which runs the `layoutDataType` switch and a checked add, then `isValid` with an error-union bounds check. There is no memcpy fast path even when `offset % 8 == 0`.
- `concatBooleanArray` copies the values bitmap the same way (:514-521): `if (bitAt(left.buffers[1], left.offset + i)) bitmap.setBit(values_bytes, i);`
- `nullCountForArray` (:754-766) counts nulls one bit at a time:
  ```zig
  while (i < data.length) : (i += 1) {
      const is_valid = v.isValid(data.offset + i) catch return error.InvalidInput;
  ```
  This path is hit for every sliced input, because a slice sets `null_count = null` (`array_data.zig:159`). `bitmap.countUnsetBitsInRange` (SIMD) already exists and is not used here.
- All-valid case: answered yes. `if (total_nulls == 0) return array_data.SharedBuffer.empty;` (:775) skips the allocation. When total_nulls > 0, though, the all-valid side still goes bit-by-bit through `isValidAt` instead of a memset of 0xFF.

Minimal fix (no bitmap copy helper exists anywhere in `src/`; I grepped):
```zig
// bitmap.zig
pub fn copyBits(dst: []u8, dst_off: usize, src: []const u8, src_off: usize, n: usize) void {
    if (dst_off % 8 == 0 and src_off % 8 == 0) { memcpy whole bytes; fix tail byte with mask; return; }
    per-bit fallback (or a shifted-byte loop later)
}
pub fn setBitsRange(dst, off, n) // memset middle bytes to 0xFF, mask the edges
// concat: no validity on a side -> setBitsRange; else copyBits(bytes, dst_off, v.data, data.offset, len)
// nullCountForArray: return bitmap.countUnsetBitsInRange(v.data, data.offset, data.offset + data.length);
```
Risk: low. Padding bits in the last byte must stay masked.

## 3. MED-HIGH: `validateLayout` scans offsets from 0 to `offset+length`, not just the slice window

`src/array/array_data.zig:502`: `const total_len = std.math.add(usize, self.offset, self.length)`. That value is then passed to:
- `validateOffsetsI32(offsets, total_len, data_len)` (:561), which loops `while (i < needed_len)` from index 1 (:223-228). Same for I64 (:249-262).
- `validateByteViews(self.buffers[1].data, total_len, …)` (:514), which loops `while (i < total_len)` from 0 (:277-301).
- `validateOffsetsSizesI32/I64` (:535/:539), same pattern.

So validating a small slice at the end of a large string, list or view array costs O(offset+len). Each call is O(n) and not recursive; only `validateFull` recurses (:689-690).

Callers (production code):
- `record_batch.zig:47`: `RecordBatch.init`, every column of every batch. This includes `RecordBatchBuilder.finish` via `record_batch.zig:206`.
- `concat_array_refs.zig`: every merge step (see finding 1).
- `ipc/stream_reader.zig`: 1345, 1870, 1949, 2000, 2053, 2074, 2124, 2170, 2247, 2324.
- `ffi/c_data.zig:799` and `ffi/c_stream.zig:220`.

Not called by any builder `finish()`, and not called by any slice path.

Minimal fix: validate only the window.
```zig
// before: validateOffsetsI32(offsets, total_len, data_len)
// after:  validateOffsetsI32(offsets[self.offset..], self.length, data_len)  // after checking offsets.len >= total_len+1
// views:  validateByteViews(view_bytes[self.offset*16..], self.length, variadic)
// list_view: same, using offsets[self.offset..] and sizes[self.offset..]
```
Risk: offsets before the window are no longer checked. Elements outside the window are never accessed, so this matches Arrow C++ behaviour, but it does loosen the current contract.

## 4. MEDIUM: Builder `reset()` does not keep capacity, and the validity bitmap stays allocated after the first null

`finish()` hands each buffer over via `OwnedBuffer.toShared`, which ends with `self.data = empty_storage[0..];` (`buffer.zig:194`). Then `reset()` only clears counters. `PrimitiveBuilder.reset` (`primitive_array.zig:89-94`) is commented "Reset state while retaining reusable capacity when possible." but does only:
```zig
self.len = 0; self.null_count = 0; self.state = .ready;
```
- Capacity: after `finishReset`, the next batch starts at 0 bytes and regrows from scratch. With the planned geometric growth that is about log₂(n) reallocs plus memset per batch, on every batch.
- Sticky validity: `self.validity` stays non-null (an emptied buffer). In every later batch, each `append` goes through `array_utils.setValidBit` → `ensureBitmapCapacity` → `resize`. `finish` then emits an all-ones validity buffer with `null_count == 0` (:136), even for batches with no nulls.

The same pattern exists in `string_array.zig:111-121`, `binary_array`, `list_array.zig:136-146`, `boolean_array.zig:79-84`, `dictionary_array.zig:114-119`, `view_array.zig:291-297`, and `advanced_array.zig:477-481` / `:583-587`.

Minimal fix:
```zig
// finish(): const cap = self.values.len(); ... toShared ...; self.last_cap = cap;
// reset():  if (self.validity) |*v| v.deinit(); self.validity = null;
//           self.values = try OwnedBuffer.init(self.allocator, self.last_cap);  // reset becomes !void
// string/list: also restore offsets[0] = 0 after the re-init
```
Risk: `reset` would gain an `OutOfMemory` error. Doing the re-init lazily on first append avoids that signature change.
